examples.ko: 정부 당국자는 아직 공식 입장을 밝히지 않았어요.
examples.en: The government official has not yet stated an official position.
I spoke directly with the official in charge on the phone.

examples.ko: 익명을 요구한 당국자가 사고 원인을 설명했어요.
examples.en: An official who asked to remain anonymous explained the cause of the accident.
Is what the official in the article said true?
The diplomatic officials have decided to meet tomorrow.

examples.ko: 당국자에게 직접 물어보면 빠를 것 같아요.
examples.en: It would probably be quicker to ask the official directly.

explain: 뉴스에서 '정부 당국자', '관계 당국자'처럼 이름을 밝히지 않고 담당 기관 사람을 가리킬 때 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '담당자'나 '관계자'라고 해요.
explain_en: In the news it appears in phrases like '정부 당국자' or '관계 당국자' to refer to someone from the responsible agency without giving a name. In daily talk people say '담당자' or '관계자'.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 사장님께 의견을 말하다니 정말 당돌해요.
examples.en: A new employee giving an opinion to the CEO is really bold.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어른 앞에서도 당돌하게 자기 생각을 말해요.
examples.en: That child states their own thoughts boldly even in front of adults.
The teacher smiled for a moment at the bold question.

examples.ko: 당돌해 보이지만 사실은 속이 따뜻한 친구예요.
examples.en: She seems daring, but she is actually warm-hearted.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 사람한테 그렇게 말하다니 좀 당돌했어요.
examples.en: It was a bit forward to talk like that to someone you just met.

examples.ko: 그렇게 당돌하던 아이가 오늘은 말이 없네요.
examples.en: The child who was so bold is quiet today.

explain: 주로 나이가 어리거나 지위가 낮은 사람이 겁 없이 말하고 행동할 때 써요. 칭찬일 수도 있고 버릇없다는 뜻일 수도 있어서 말투와 상황을 봐야 해요. '당차다'는 좀 더 긍정적으로 들려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when someone young or junior speaks and acts fearlessly. It can be praise or a hint of rudeness, so tone and context matter. '당차다' sounds more positive.

examples.ko: 이 음료는 당류가 너무 많아서 자주 못 마셔요.
examples.en: This drink has too much sugar, so I can't drink it often.
The sugar content is written on the package.

examples.ko: 당류를 줄이려고 요즘 단 음료를 안 마셔요.
examples.en: I've stopped drinking sweet drinks lately to cut down on sugar.

examples.ko: 과일에 들어 있는 당류도 너무 많이 먹으면 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Even the sugars in fruit are not good if you eat too much.
I check the sugar on the nutrition label first.
I'm curious about the recommended daily amount of sugar.

explain: 영양 성분표나 식품 설명에서 보는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '설탕'이나 '단 것'이라고 많이 말해요. 당류에는 설탕뿐 아니라 포도당, 과당 같은 것도 들어가요.
explain_en: You see it on nutrition labels and food explanations. In daily talk people say '설탕' or '단 것'. The category covers not only table sugar but also things like glucose and fructose.

examples.en: The countries involved in the dispute sat down at the negotiating table.
They say dialogue between the countries concerned is needed.
This problem has to be solved by the countries involved themselves.

examples.ko: 당사국의 동의 없이는 결정할 수 없어요.
examples.en: A decision can't be made without the consent of the country concerned.
The two countries are parties to that agreement.

examples.ko: 당사국이 아닌 나라는 의견만 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Countries that are not parties can only offer opinions.

explain: 조약이나 분쟁에 직접 관련된 나라를 말할 때 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 직접 관련 없는 나라는 '제3국'이라고 해요. 나라가 아니라 사람이나 회사일 때는 '당사자'를 써요.
explain_en: It appears often in the news for a country directly involved in a treaty or dispute. A country not directly involved is a '제3국'. For people or companies, use '당사자' instead.

examples.ko: 이번 조사에서 그 후보는 당선권에 들었어요.
examples.en: In this poll, that candidate is within winning range.
Since I was outside the winning range, I was nervous until the end.
Her ranking went up and she finally got into winning range.
Everyone was disappointed by the news that we had fallen out of winning range.

examples.ko: 당선권인지 아닌지는 개표 후에 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: We can only know whether it's winning range after the votes are counted.
He narrowly stayed within winning range.

explain: '당선권에 들다', '당선권 밖'처럼 선거 뉴스에서 많이 나오는 말이에요. 비례대표 순번 이야기에서도 자주 들려요. 후보의 순위나 지지율이 당선될 만한 자리인지 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It shows up in election news in phrases like '당선권에 들다' and '당선권 밖'. It is also common when talking about proportional representation list positions. Use it when asking whether a candidate's rank or support is high enough to win.

examples.en: This year's contest winners were announced.
This poster was last year's winning entry.
I saw the winning works in person at the exhibition hall.
The winning work will be published as a book.
I'm curious about the judges' comments on the winning work.
My painting was chosen as a winning entry!

explain: 공모전이나 신춘문예처럼 작품을 모집해서 뽑을 때 써요. 상을 받은 작품 전체를 말하는 '수상작'과 달리, 공모에서 뽑힌 작품이라는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: Use it for works chosen in an open call, such as contests or the New Year literary contests. Unlike '수상작', which covers any award-winning work, it strongly suggests a work selected from submissions.

examples.ko: 부모님이 도와주시는 걸 당연시하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't take it for granted that your parents help you.
People take a convenient life too much for granted.

examples.ko: 그는 남의 친절을 당연시하는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: He has a habit of taking other people's kindness for granted.

examples.ko: 야근을 당연시했던 분위기가 이제 바뀌고 있어요.
examples.en: The atmosphere that took overtime for granted is now changing.

examples.ko: 감사하는 마음을 잃고 모든 걸 당연시하게 됐어요.
examples.en: I lost my sense of gratitude and started taking everything for granted.

examples.ko: 여자니까 집안일을 해야 한다고 당연시하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't assume as a given that she must do housework because she is a woman.

explain: '~을/를 당연시하다' 형태로 쓰고, 고마워해야 할 일을 그냥 당연하게 여긴다는 비판의 느낌이 자주 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '당연하게 여기다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used as '~을/를 당연시하다' and often carries a hint of criticism, as in not being grateful for something. In everyday talk people also say '당연하게 여기다'.

examples.en: You studied hard, so passing is only natural.

examples.ko: 값이 오르면 수요가 줄어드는 게 당연지사죠.
examples.en: When prices go up, demand falling is a matter of course.

examples.ko: 그렇게 늦게 자면 피곤한 게 당연지사 아니에요?
examples.en: If you sleep that late, isn't being tired only natural?
Don't accept it as a given; you should be grateful.
It was only natural that the boss got angry too.
I thought it was a matter of course, but it seems it wasn't.

explain: '~는 당연지사예요'처럼 문장 끝에서 많이 써요. 조금 딱딱한 한자어 느낌이라 일상 대화에서는 '당연한 일이에요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is often used at the end of a sentence, as in '~는 당연지사예요'. It sounds a little stiff, so in everyday talk people say '당연한 일이에요'.

examples.ko: 이 정책이 꼭 필요한 당위성을 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Please explain why this policy is necessary and justified.

examples.ko: 환경을 지켜야 한다는 당위성은 누구나 알아요.
examples.en: Everyone knows we ought to protect the environment.

examples.ko: 당위성만 말하지 말고 방법도 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Don't just talk about why we should; tell us how, too.
His argument lacks a sense of necessity.
Opinions were divided on whether the plan was justified.
The 'ought to' matters, but you also have to look at reality.

explain: '그렇게 해야 마땅하다'는 이유를 말할 때 토론이나 글에서 많이 써요. '필요성'은 필요한 이유이고, 당위성은 옳기 때문에 해야 한다는 쪽에 더 가까워요. 일상 대화보다는 논설이나 발표에서 들려요.
explain_en: It is used in debates and writing for the reason something ought to be done. '필요성' is the reason something is needed, while 당위성 leans toward doing it because it is right. You hear it more in essays and presentations than in daily talk.

examples.en: I have no idea what you're talking about.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 당최 어떻게 쓰는지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I can't figure out how to use this machine at all.

examples.ko: 그 사람 속을 당최 알 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I can never tell what's on that person's mind.

examples.ko: 왜 그러는지 당최 이해가 안 돼요.
examples.en: I just can't understand why he's doing that.
These days I have no appetite at all, and it's hard.

examples.ko: 길이 복잡해서 당최 어디가 어딘지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: The roads are so complicated that I can't tell where anything is.

explain: '모르겠다', '안 되다', '없다'처럼 부정적인 말과 함께 써서 '전혀, 도무지'라는 느낌을 강하게 줘요. 말할 때 많이 쓰는 구어체이고, 글에서는 '도무지'나 '전혀'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It goes with negative expressions such as '모르겠다', '안 되다' and '없다' to give a strong sense of 'not at all'. It is a spoken, colloquial word; in writing '도무지' or '전혀' are more common.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 질문에 당혹감을 감출 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't hide my bewilderment at the sudden question.
A wave of bewilderment came over me when I heard the news.
I was so flustered that I couldn't speak.
He had a look of being engulfed in confusion.
The confusion quickly turned into laughter.
It was so strange that it even left me bewildered.

explain: 뜻밖의 일 때문에 어쩔 줄 몰라 하는 마음이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '당황스럽다'가 더 자주 나오고, 당혹감은 '느끼다', '감추다', '휩싸이다'와 함께 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of not knowing what to do because of something unexpected. In daily talk '당황스럽다' is more common, while 당혹감 appears in writing and news with verbs like '느끼다', '감추다' and '휩싸이다'.

examples.en: The Great Depression began in the United States in 1929.

examples.ko: 대공황 때 많은 사람이 일자리를 잃었어요.
examples.en: Many people lost their jobs during the Great Depression.
We learned about the Great Depression in history class.

examples.ko: 지금 경제 상황이 대공황과 비슷하다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: Some say the current economy is similar to the Great Depression.

examples.ko: 대공황을 겪은 세대는 돈을 아껴 쓰는 편이에요.
examples.en: The generation that lived through the Great Depression tends to spend money carefully.
Economists studied the causes of the Great Depression for a long time.

explain: 보통 1930년대 세계 경제를 무너뜨린 대공황을 가리켜요. 그냥 경기가 나쁜 '불황'보다 훨씬 심각한 위기라는 느낌이에요. '세계 대공황'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It usually refers to the crash that shook the world economy in the 1930s. It feels much more severe than an ordinary downturn, '불황'. People also often say '세계 대공황'.

en: on earth; what in the world

examples.en: What on earth happened?
Who on earth did this?
How long on earth do I have to wait?
Gosh, how long has it been!
Tell me what on earth the problem is.
Where on earth did it all go wrong?

explain: 궁금하거나 답답한 마음을 강조하는 말이라 '도대체'와 비슷하지만, 좀 더 예스럽고 글 느낌이 나요. 일상 대화에서는 '도대체'나 '대체'를 더 많이 써요. 보통 의문문에서 써요.
explain_en: It stresses curiosity or frustration and is similar to '도대체', but it sounds more old-fashioned and bookish. In daily talk '도대체' or '대체' are more common. It is usually used in questions.

examples.en: The puppy rolls around on the floor.
The ball rolled down the hill.
My stomach hurt so much I felt like rolling around.
The baby plays rolling around on the bed.

examples.ko: 도토리가 대굴대굴 굴러서 잡을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The acorn rolled away and I couldn't catch it.
The marble rolls around on the desk.

explain: 작고 단단한 것이 구르는 모양을 흉내 낸 말이에요. 보통 '대굴대굴 구르다', '대굴대굴 굴러가다'로 써요. '데굴데굴'과 같은 계열이라 소리와 느낌이 비슷해요.
explain_en: It imitates the way something small and hard rolls. It is usually used as '대굴대굴 구르다' or '대굴대굴 굴러가다'. It belongs to the same family as '데굴데굴', so the sound and feel are similar.

examples.en: The spacecraft re-entered the atmosphere.
The rocket left the atmosphere and flew into space.
From outside the atmosphere, Earth looks blue.
Most meteoroids burn up in the atmosphere.

examples.ko: 위성이 대기권으로 진입할 때 매우 뜨거워져요.
examples.en: A satellite gets extremely hot when it enters the atmosphere.
The atmosphere surrounds the Earth.

explain: 우주나 지구과학 이야기에서 많이 나와요. '대기권 밖', '대기권 진입', '대기권을 벗어나다'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서 날씨를 말할 때는 그냥 '공기'나 '하늘'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It comes up often in talk about space and earth science, in phrases like '대기권 밖', '대기권 진입' and '대기권을 벗어나다'. When talking about everyday weather, people just say '공기' or '하늘'.

en: being domestic and foreign; being home and abroad; being internal and external

examples.en: I'm worried because conditions at home and abroad are difficult.
It is facing criticism from both inside and outside.
The company announced its new plan internally and externally.
It was a year with many difficulties both at home and abroad.
We need a strategy that covers both internal and external matters.
It received good reviews both inside and outside.

explain: 나라나 조직의 안과 밖을 함께 말할 때 쓰는 뉴스·보고서 말투예요. 일상 대화에서는 '안팎'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a news and report style word for the inside and outside of a country or organization together. In daily talk people say '안팎'.

examples.en: We have to overcome the crisis both at home and abroad.
Internal and external conditions are not good.
The plan was postponed because of internal and external factors.
Assessments at home and abroad are divided.
Building trust both inside and outside is important.
It is a difficult time both domestically and internationally.

explain: '대내외적 위기'처럼 명사 앞에 쓰고, '대내외적으로' 형태의 부사로도 많이 써요. 나라뿐 아니라 회사나 단체의 안팎에도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '안팎으로'가 더 자연스럽고, '대내외적'은 뉴스나 발표에서 자주 들리는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '대내외적 위기', and is also common as the adverb '대내외적으로'. It applies to the inside and outside of a company or group as well as a country. In daily talk '안팎으로' sounds more natural, while '대내외적' is a stiff expression often heard in news and presentations.

examples.ko: 긴 드라마가 드디어 대단원의 막을 내렸어요.
examples.en: The long drama finally came to its finale.
The movie ends with a happy finale.
All the misunderstandings are cleared up in the finale.
The long project is nearing its end.
The actors shed tears ahead of the finale.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 대단원이 너무 급하게 끝나요.
examples.en: This novel's ending wraps up too hurriedly.

explain: 연극, 소설, 드라마의 마지막 부분을 말할 때 쓰고, 오래 이어진 일의 끝에도 비유로 써요. 주로 '대단원의 막을 내리다'로 말해요. 가벼운 대화에서는 '마지막'이나 '결말'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 십 년간 이어진 시리즈가 대단원의 막을 내렸어요.
phrases.en: The series that ran for ten years has come to a close.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연극이 끝나고 막이 내려오는 모습에서 나온 말로, 오래 이어진 일이나 이야기가 마무리될 때 써요. 격식 있는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: It comes from the curtain falling at the end of a play, and is used when a long-running event or story wraps up. It sounds formal.
phrases.en_equiv: bring down the curtain; come to a close

explain_en: It refers to the last part of a play, novel or drama, and is also used figuratively for the end of a long-running matter. It is mostly said as '대단원의 막을 내리다'. In casual talk people say '마지막' or '결말'.
